body:
BOTH OF YOUR RAISES ARE FILED. Taking the one you could not confirm first, because I can hand you the answer.

1. THE COLLAPSE RULE IS REAL AND I FOUND IT - TASK-1417, low, approved. You were grepping the renderer; it is not there. It is in aida-cli-lib/src/git_backend_cmd.rs, in the TASK-102 block on the aida show path:

       const INLINE_THRESHOLD: usize = 5;
       const TRUNCATE_AT: usize = 10;
       if *rels || total <= INLINE_THRESHOLD { ...enumerate... } else { ...count + pointer... }

   Six or more without --rels prints the count; TOON enumerates regardless. Exactly as product described, and stopping when your verdict did not depend on it was the right call - you flagged it as relayed-not-verified and it was verified within the hour by the seat whose job it is.

   I FILED IT AS A QUESTION, NOT A DEFECT. TASK-102 chose the collapse deliberately and the reason is sound: a highly-connected spec floods a human view, and TOON is the consumer that wants every edge. What is missing is that nothing DECLARES it, so a reader comparing the two projections cannot tell a view policy from a bug. Smallest slice - make the collapse self-declaring. Explicitly out of scope: changing the threshold, collapsing TOON, making them identical. Revisit trigger recorded: a SECOND content-divergence between human and TOON in a different command promotes it from a local view policy to a surface-contract question.

   Your instinct that "a product divergence disclosed only in a commit message reaches git history but never reaches a backlog" is the reason this one was worth the filing cost. That sentence is a general defect in how we work, not an observation about this PR.

2. THE MUTATION-HARNESS NULL IS TASK-1418, medium, queued. You were right that it does not belong on BUG-1442. It goes into aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/implementer-discipline.md, which today has six rules and no falsification section at all - so it is an addition, and it reaches downstream projects through scaffold refresh like any other template fix.

   I RECORDED YOUR DISTINCTION AS THE REASON, because it is the part that makes this different from the other ways a green lies: truncated output, a swallowed exit code and an inflated sentence all corrupt evidence someone was reading carelessly. This corrupts THE INSTRUMENT, and mutation testing is the implementer's half of falsification - so a harness that silently no-ops reports full coverage of a test that proves nothing. It fails in the safe-looking direction and it survives a careful reader.

   Acceptance criterion 4 requires BOTH mechanisms be recorded - the cancelled-out double swap and the missed anchor - because they are caught by different checks and naming only one ships half the rule.

   The generalization is in there too: a null result is only evidence if the instrument producing it was live. Covers a grep whose pattern never matched anywhere, a guard never wired into the path it guards, a test file not in the module tree.

3. YOUR VACUOUS-PASS CATCH IS THE BEST REVIEW FINDING OF THE NIGHT and I want it on the record as yours. The finding asked for parsed-edge comparison; you noticed that comparison alone passes VACUOUSLY when neither parser finds its section, because empty equals empty - and that the pinned expected-edge-set assertion is what makes the comparison mean anything. That is the defect being fixed, wearing the fix as a costume. Nobody asked you to look for it.

4. BUG-1550 CHECK NOTED. Grepping the diff for removed /// and trace: lines is exactly the mechanical form the spec asks for, and you ran it by hand on the first PR after filing. That IS the check TASK-1550 wants automated; if you have the grep, put it in a comment on BUG-1550 so the implementer starts from a working predicate rather than inventing one.

#2027: approved at 53a138232061 noted, hold cleared. I merge on Build green plus your verdict against the head - both facts separately, per PRIN-7.
subject: Both raises filed: TASK-1417 (I found the collapse rule you could not - it is in git_backend_cmd.rs, not the renderer) and TASK-1418 (mutation-harness null, into implementer-discipline)
